root_idea.summary: The root centers on taking up something seen on the ground, often unexpectedly, though the taking may also be deliberate.
root_idea.development: From physical picking up or finding, the lexical development extends to found property, foundlings, gleanings, mineral finds, unexpected discovery, and related agentive, locative, and figurative usages.

senses.definition: To pick up, take up, or collect a person or thing found.
senses.usage_conditions: Used transitively for taking up or collecting what has been encountered or found; the Quranic occurrences include taking up a person.

senses.definition: To come upon or find unexpectedly, without seeking.
senses.usage_conditions: A Form VIII construction describing an unplanned discovery; the taking up may follow the unexpected encounter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pick up, take up, or raise something from the ground, or to take something from a place where it was not expected.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The basic Form I usage; it may describe taking something deliberately or finding and taking it without prior expectation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To acquire knowledge or information piecemeal from different books or sources.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage with knowledge or learning as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut off a person's fingers without cutting away the main part of the hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized transitive usage describing partial removal by cutting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse's lifting all its legs together in a rapid pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical equestrian term, applied to the paces called تَقْرِيب and خَبَب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Being opposite or facing one another; meeting face to face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of places that face one another and of people who meet directly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pick up dates or fruits from one place after another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V usage emphasizing repeated or distributed picking from scattered places.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing picked up or taken from the ground; found or lost property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for an object obtained by picking it up, including property found after being dropped or left.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Scattered, fallen, or paltry things left for anyone to pick up.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes things of little worth that have fallen or been left behind, including dates gathered from the stumps of palm branches.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Gleanings of grain or fruit collected after the main harvest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially ears of grain missed by the reaping hooks and subsequently picked up.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pieces of gold or silver found in a mine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of mineral pieces discovered in the ground, especially valuable pieces found in a mine.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small quantity of pasture or forage available in a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of sparse herbage available for grazing animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who repeatedly seeks out and picks up things.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported usage for a persistent picker; it is distinct from the more common noun meaning found property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of gleaning ears of grain missed by the reaping hooks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Names the activity of picking up what remains after harvesting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing picked up or taken from the ground; found property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial noun for something found and taken up, including found property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A foundling or abandoned child who is found and taken up.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional noun for a child cast out or abandoned and subsequently found; its parentage is unknown in the standard description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well discovered unexpectedly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage for a well upon which one lights without seeking it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A low, ignoble, base, or mean person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man or woman in a figurative, depreciative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who picks up things, especially a gleaner of fallen grain or fruit; also a bird that picks up grains.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The agent noun may describe ordinary or frequent picking, including gathering ears missed at harvest and fruit fallen from the raceme.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who catches up, repeats, and spreads words that have been uttered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage in the proverb لِكُلِّ سَاقِطَةٍ لَاقِطَةٌ, literally associating every uttered saying with someone who picks it up.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The digestive stomach or omasum in which earth and pebbles collect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to the relevant stomach of a bird, sheep, goat, or camel because it gathers what the animal eats of earth and pebbles.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A freedman or emancipated slave; also the slave of a freedman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized social-status usage, with related kinship terminology formed from لاقط and its paired terms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small number of people who are separated, scattered, or dispersed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective plural usage describing people in scattered groups.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The refuse, lowest, basest, or meanest sort of people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural usage for a degraded social class or group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where something is picked up or sought; a place of discovery, including a mine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A locative noun for a place in which something is to be found or searched for.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An implement with which something is picked up or taken from the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tool noun for an instrument used to seize or lift an object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tweezers or a pincers-like instrument used to pluck hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized instrumental usage, identified with the implement called مِنْقَاش.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vile, mean, paltry, or contemptible thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival usage equivalent to a term for something fallen or debased.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form I physical, figurative acquisitive, and specialized cutting usages are represented.
Facing and face-to-face meeting meaning represented.
Form VIII collection meaning represented under the Quranic verb.
Unexpected discovery meaning represented under the Quranic verb.
The unit contains several nominal branches, all represented.
Lowest or basest people usage represented.
Illustrative pasture example; it adds no independent lexical branch.
The found-property expression is covered by the picked-up object meaning.
Vile or paltry thing meaning represented.

cautions: The packet contains no unique Mufradat entry for this root; the Quranic lexical senses are therefore based on the Form VIII lexical evidence together with the securely identified QAC occurrences.
